title: February 4 Luanda demonstration demanding political alternation
location: Luanda; Novo Jornal S009 places the group near Estatua do Motorista on Avenida Deolinda Rodrigues and reports a route toward 1º de Maio. Its S004 follow-up also says 1º de Maio but quotes an activist naming Largo da Independência. VOA Portuguese S015 places the assembly at Cemitério Sant’Ana and a route toward the Presidential Palace. These site/route accounts remain unresolved.
organizer: Sociedade Civil Contestatária (named by both reports)
participants_original: Novo Jornal reports 150–200 youths; VOA Portuguese says nearly 200 activists.
threshold_50_evidence: Novo Jornal explicitly reports between 150 and 200 youths at the demonstration; VOA's separate 'nearly 200' description is consistent but not converted to an exact count.

title.summary: Three opened reports describe the February 4 Luanda action by Sociedade Civil Contestatária; the two Novo Jornal articles are from one publisher, while VOA has a distinct byline.

start_date.summary: S004 gives February 4, 2021 at 16:57; S009 and S015 also place the march on February 4. The publications’ dates are not used as substitute occurrence dates.

location.summary: S009 gives the meeting near Estatua do Motorista/Avenida Deolinda Rodrigues and intended arrival at 1º de Maio. S004 also names 1º de Maio but quotes Largo da Independência. VOA S015 places assembly at Cemitério Sant’Ana and a Presidential Palace route. It is unclear whether these describe stages of one moving march or different meeting/route accounts.

scope.summary: Both reports describe local action in Luanda.

organizer.summary: All three reports name Sociedade Civil Contestatária as the organizer.

demands.summary: Reports identify demands for political alternation and the MPLA to leave power; S004 also describes better living conditions. No narrower price or wage category is established.

participants_original.summary: S009 reports 150–200 youths; VOA S015 says nearly 200; S004 says several youths and provides no crowd total. Estimates are not added.

participants_min.summary: Explicit lower endpoint 150 from Novo Jornal.

participants_max.summary: Explicit upper endpoint 200 from Novo Jornal.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Novo Jornal S009 explicitly reports 150–200 youths; VOA S015’s qualitative near-200 account is consistent but not an exact count. S004 supplies no total.

protester_violence.summary: VOA reports burning-tire barricades but no injury or property-damage outcome; violence remains unknown pending consistent coding.

end_date.summary: S004 says police frustrated the march and S009 reports tear gas used to disperse remaining demonstrators, but none establishes that all physical assembly ended that day; end remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Neither report describes the State receiving or accommodating demands.

state_response.arrests.summary: S009 reports more than two dozen detentions before the march began; S004 and S015 report additional/during-action detentions. Detentions are response evidence, not crowd turnout.

state_response.beatings.summary: VOA reports police beat activists and quotes Geraldo Dala describing his beating; claims remain attributed.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: S004 says police used shots and tear gas to prevent the march; S009 explicitly says tear gas was used to disperse those remaining. The reports establish an attributed attempt to prevent/disperse the crowd.

state_response.ignore.summary: No explicit refusal or avoidance of demands is reported.

state_response.killings.summary: The opened event reports describe injuries but no death attributable to this action; the response field remains unknown rather than a sourced no.

state_response.shootings.summary: Novo Jornal S004 explicitly reports that the National Police used shots and that two youths were struck by gunfire in the legs. This is attributed shooting evidence from one outlet; it is not inferred from S009’s earlier report that shots were heard.

notes: The February 4 event is reported by two contemporaneous outlets with different bylines: Novo Jornal says it was on site; VOA Portuguese names Coque Mukuta and no wire source in the body. Both identify the same organizer, date, slogan and domestic political target; they report different starting/meeting points and intended routes (1º de Maio vs Presidential Palace), which may reflect one march at different points or unresolved site boundaries. Preserve both accounts and do not split or sum attendance. Pre-march detentions are response evidence, not participant counts. January Cafunfo casualties/violence are motivating context, not responses to this Luanda event. S004 is a second Novo Jornal article from the same publisher; it explicitly attributes gunfire and tear gas to the National Police and reports two youths struck in the legs. This supports state_response.shootings=yes on that attributed account. The article also reports arrests and hospital access limits. The S004 and S009 reports are not independent corroboration; VOA S015 is distinct but does not identify a written wire source. The article’s destination wording is itself inconsistent (1º de Maio and Largo da Independência).
open_questions: Clarify whether the reported Luanda meeting points and destination wording refer to one moving march or different gathering/route accounts.
Determine whether police dispersal ended all physical assembly that day; end_date remains null.

Seek independent confirmation and identify the two reported injured youths and any later medical/court follow-up; shootings=yes rests on S004’s explicit National Police attribution, while S009 alone only reports heard shots.
Assess what burning-tire barricades mean for the protester_violence field under the protocol.
Do not transfer January Cafunfo casualties to this Luanda action.
